headline: Sox Return To Fenway Looking To Keep The Streak Alive
morning_brew: We are back at Fenway tonight after a decent road trip, and this squad is actually carrying a three-game winning streak into this series against Minnesota. Look, a twenty-two and twenty-seven record is nothing to throw a parade for, but at least the bats finally showed some signs of life out on the road. The Twins are sitting at twenty-three and twenty-seven, so this is a prime opportunity to gain some ground and show this city they actually want to compete. Let us hope the energy is right when they take the field under the lights.

With the summer months approaching, all the national writers are already speculating about the trade deadline and who might be on the move. Boston has always been a town that expects to contend, and we have nine titles in the trophy case to prove it, but this current group has a lot of questions to answer before management decides to make any big moves. If we can put together a strong run over the next few weeks, maybe ownership makes a real splash. If they keep hovering below five hundred, it is going to be a very quiet July.

Meanwhile, the local basketball and hockey scene is dead quiet with both the Celtics and Bruins watching the playoffs from their couches. It still stings to think about those early exits, but the rumor mill is already grinding with talk about free agent rankings and draft assets. The Celtics have eighteen banners hanging in the rafters, so anything less than a deep run is a massive disappointment in this town. It is going to be a long, hot summer of speculation, but right now, my focus is entirely on the diamond.
